title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's manuscript notes on motives and Hodge theory (c. 1969-72). The page sits between two upside-down Bourbaki typescript pages on Dedekind rings, which are just scrap paper.

Setting (as far as it can be read):
- k/k_0 is a Galois extension of number fields and M is a motive over k.
- For each archimedean place / complex embedding v: k -> C there is a Betti lattice M_v^Z = H_B(M ⊗_v C, Z).
- There are also the l-adic realizations M_l for finite l, and an 'infinite' realization M_K(∞) with coefficients in some field K. K is probably R or C; it is unclear from the image.
- G is a group attached to M: its motivic Galois group, or Mumford-Tate-type group, apparently with an integral structure G(Z). The page says G is connected.

The crossed-out opening line fixed one infinite place v of k_0, i.e. an embedding k -> C up to conjugation. Grothendieck then considers σ ∈ Gal(k/k_0) acting on the conjugate embeddings v ↦ σv. The finite components of the action are the Galois maps σ_l on the l-adic realizations.

The new point, underlined twice with '!!!': in the product σ_* = ((σ_l)_{l finite}, σ_∞), the archimedean component σ_∞ is now a well-determined element of G(K). This gives a unique map φ_v: Gal(k/k_0) -> G(K) ⊂ GL(M_K(∞)) characterised by
 M^Z_{σv} = σ_* M^Z_v, with σ_* = ((σ_l)_l, φ_v(σ)).
In words: the Betti lattice for the conjugate embedding is the transform of the lattice for v by the finite-adelic Galois action, corrected at infinity by a unique element of the group G.

From uniqueness he derives the twisted cocycle rule φ_v(τσ) = ^τφ_v(σ) · φ_v(τ). Setting ψ_v = φ_v^{-1}, this becomes the standard 1-cocycle (crossed homomorphism) condition ψ_v(τσ) = ψ_v(τ) · ^τψ_v(σ).

An N.B. adds that G may be regarded as a group defined over k_0, independent of v. This is Galois descent of the group via the cocycle.

Purpose: to describe how the Betti realizations at the different complex embeddings of k are related, given that there is no algebraic isomorphism between them. The answer is a Galois 1-cocycle with values in the motivic group, whose finite-adelic part is the l-adic Galois action. This is the problem later treated by Deligne (absolute Hodge cycles, the comparison H_B(X)⊗A_f ≅ H_B(σX)⊗A_f; the Taniyama group), Langlands (conjugation of Shimura varieties), and Milne–Shih.
errors: Existence and uniqueness of φ_v(σ) in G(K) are asserted, not proved. Existence requires that the composite of the Galois maps σ_l with the comparison isomorphisms respects all motivic tensors (Deligne's absolute Hodge property, or the Hodge/Tate conjectures). Uniqueness presumably uses that an element is determined by its effect on lattices, together with G being connected or having trivial centre-type ambiguity; this is not justified on the page and may only hold modulo the centre or modulo G(Z).
The coefficient field K and the precise realization M_K(∞) are not specified. Whether φ_v(σ) can really be taken in G(Q), G(R) or G(C) matters, and is unclear.

The cocycle formula's ordering depends on left/right action conventions. Inverting does correctly convert the twisted rule into the standard crossed-homomorphism rule, so the computation itself is consistent.

ideas.what: Betti lattices for conjugate complex embeddings are related by the finite-adelic Galois action combined with a unique archimedean element of the motivic/Mumford-Tate group
ideas.modern_name: Conjugation of motives / absolute Hodge comparison H_B(X)⊗A_f ≅ H_B(σX)⊗A_f; ingredient of the Taniyama group and of Langlands' conjugation conjecture for Shimura varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, LNM 900, 1982); Langlands (1979); Milne–Shih (1982)

ideas.what: The map σ ↦ φ_v(σ) is a (twisted) Galois 1-cocycle with values in G; G descends to k_0 independently of v
ideas.modern_name: Galois cocycle / descent of the motivic Galois group; analogue of the cocycle defining the Taniyama group extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Langlands; Deligne ('Motifs et groupes de Taniyama', 1982)

ideas.what: Inverting a twisted cocycle gives a standard crossed homomorphism

missed.claim: Around 1970 Grothendieck already formulates the comparison of Betti realizations at conjugate embeddings as a unique G-valued Galois cocycle, whose finite components are l-adic Galois actions and whose infinite component lies in the motivic group. This anticipates the structure of Deligne–Langlands' Taniyama group and the conjugation problem for Shimura varieties by about a decade.
missed.quote: où maintenant σ_∞ est un élément bien déterminé de G(K)!!! ... M^Z_{σv} = σ_* M^Z_v ... σ_* = ((σ_l)_{l fini}, φ_v(σ))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents an early, integral (lattice-level) Grothendieck formulation of the 'conjugation of motives' cocycle. The integral version, with G over Z and lattices, is somewhat sharper than the usual rational statements and is of historical interest for the genesis of the Taniyama group.

missed.claim: The cocycle φ_v and the descent of G to k_0 are introduced but not exploited: no class in H^1, no extension group of Gal by G, and no proof of existence or uniqueness.
missed.quote: N.B. G peut être considéré comme groupe défini sur k_0 (indépendant de v!)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the natural route to a Taniyama-type extension 1 -> G -> T -> Gal -> 1 for general (not only CM) motives. That route is still largely conjectural.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clear, emphasised early formulation of the Galois-conjugation cocycle for Betti lattices with values in the motivic group, a structure later central to Deligne's and Langlands' work around 1979-82. However, it is sketchy, depends on unproved hypotheses, and Grothendieck's broader motivic Galois ideas are already known to have inspired that work.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'On sait que G est connexe ...', concerning G with integral structure G(Z); the rest is illegible.
The underlined passage reads 'où maintenant σ_∞ est un élément bien déterminé de G(K)!!!' (not 'homomorphisme').
Before the box: 'On obtient ainsi un homomorphisme unique', i.e. the map Gal(k/k_0) -> G_*(K) ⊂ GL(M_K(∞)) labelled φ_v.
The cocycle line should read 'On vérifie aussitôt φ_v(τσ) = ^τφ_v(σ) φ_v(τ)', and the next line 'ou en posant ψ_v = φ_v^{-1}: ψ_v(τσ) = ψ_v(τ) ^τψ_v(σ)'.
The crossed-out first lines read approximately 'Fixons une v de k_0 infinie, i.e. une classe de plongements k -> C (mod conjugaison complexe)'.
